## About

Service Architect is a visual designer and code generator for distributed systems. You draw a graph of services, typed pipelines, and connections; the designer generates the Python project, transport adapters, configuration, observability wiring, and runtime graph.

This repository is the Python 3.12+ runtime used by that generated code. It preserves the observable stream, cancellation, lifecycle, configuration, and connector semantics of the Go reference implementation while using asyncio, aiohttp, grpcio, and aiokafka.

> **The graph is the architecture. It runs the system and remains accurate by definition.**

ServiceLib is normally consumed through generated projects rather than assembled by hand.

→ **[Open Service Architect](https://www.gorundebug.com)**

---

## What The Runtime Provides

- Typed generated stream graphs for Python 3.12+
- asyncio-based execution and lifecycle management
- Function-call, task-pool, priority-pool, and parallel call semantics
- HTTP, gRPC, Kafka, and local in-process connectors
- Deadlines, cancellation propagation, delay pools, and graceful shutdown
- In-memory join state with rotating retention maps
- OpenTelemetry traces and logs, Prometheus-compatible metrics, and status endpoints
- Generated configuration models, environment substitution, and values-file hot reload

Graph construction, consumer resolution, middleware composition, and metric creation happen during service startup. Runtime requests traverse the pre-built graph.

---

## Execution Model

| Semantics | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `FunctionCall` | Await the next consumer directly; optionally schedule asynchronously |
| `TaskPool` | Schedule work on a named bounded asyncio worker pool |
| `PriorityTaskPool` | Schedule work using request priority |
| `Parallel` | Dispatch independently as an asyncio task |

Message context, payload, cancellation, deadline, priority, and tracing state are carried independently so transport-visible state can be propagated without serializing process-local scheduling details.

---

## Operators

| Operator | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Input` | Receive data from an external system |
| `Sink` | Send data to an external system |
| `Map` / `Filter` | Transform or conditionally pass values |
| `FlatMap` / `FlatMapIterable` | Expand a value into multiple outputs |
| `Process` / `Error` | Produce normal and error output streams |
| `KeyBy` | Partition values by key |
| `Join` / `MultiJoin` | Combine keyed streams |
| `Merge` / `Split` | Merge or fan out stream branches |
| `Case` / `When` | Route values conditionally |
| `Delay` | Deliver later or immediately on cancellation |
| `CycleLink` | Feed values back into the graph |

---

## Connectors

**Sources** — HTTP · gRPC · Kafka · local/custom

**Sinks** — HTTP · gRPC · Kafka · local/custom

HTTP and gRPC propagate stream identity, trace context, baggage, and remaining deadlines where supported. Process-local scheduling metadata, such as priority, stays local.

---

## Configuration And Hot Reload

At startup, generated configuration is assembled from the base YAML document, values substitution, an optional overrides document, and environment variables.

When a values file is present, ServiceLib watches it with `watchfiles`, including Kubernetes ConfigMap-style atomic symlink replacement. A successful update rebuilds the generated config model and asks the runtime and its pools to reload. Failed updates are logged and counted while the service continues running with its previous configuration.

---

## Observability

ServiceLib provides backend-neutral logging, metrics, and tracing interfaces with production OpenTelemetry/Prometheus adapters and in-memory test engines.

Automatic instrumentation covers:

- service lifecycle
- stream operators and call semantics
- task, priority, and delay pools
- source and sink endpoints
- HTTP, gRPC, and Kafka transports
- storage and join execution

Request tracing is enabled by a non-empty `X-Trace`/`x-trace` marker or an already sampled W3C remote parent. Without either signal, ServiceLib avoids creating recording request, operator, pool, source, or sink spans.

No-op metrics and logging implementations are available for benchmarks and tests that intentionally exclude observability storage.

---

## Installation

Generated projects pin the runtime version they were generated against. For local framework development:

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
```

The distribution package is named `pyservicelib_gorundebug`.

---

## Quality Checks

```sh
./linters.sh
pytest
```

The suite covers operators, pools, stores, serialization, configuration parity, HTTP/gRPC/Kafka behavior, metrics, tracing, and shutdown.
